Sounds of the harbour

Fog signal

Text alternative: one long low blast, a pause of two seconds, then two short blasts. The pattern repeats every minute.

Ferry bell

Audio description: a brass bell rings four times. Nobody speaks.

Harbour master's welcome

Welcome to the harbour. The visitor dock is on the east side, past the blue crane. Tie up at any marked berth and report to the office within the hour.

Lock gates

A horn sounds twice before the gates open, and once when they are fully shut.

Buoy

A slow clanging tone, about one strike every three seconds, with no speech.

Tide report

Mayor's welcome

This recording says the following: Welcome to the new town hall. The doors open at nine each weekday, the front desk is on your left, and the lift to the council chamber is straight ahead past the stairs.

Winter parking notice

From the first of December cars may not be left on Mill Road overnight. Snow ploughs need the whole width of the road between ten at night and six in the morning, and cars left there will be moved to the yard behind the depot at the owner's cost.

You can also listen to this notice.

Statement on the bridge works

The bridge on Ferry Lane closes to cars for six weeks from Monday. People on foot and on bicycles can cross on the east side at all times, and a free shuttle bus runs every twenty minutes from the market square to the far bank.

A word from the chair

Ferry timetable change

From Monday the first ferry leaves the east quay at half past six and the last one returns at ten at night. On Sundays the service starts an hour later, and there is no sailing on the first of January or on the day of the harbour race.

You can also listen to this notice.

Lifeboat open day

This recording says the following: The lifeboat station is open to visitors on the last Saturday of each month. Tours start on the hour from ten until three, and children must be with an adult at all times.

Tide warning

What the warning says

This recording says the following: Spring tides this week will cover the lower car park from two hours before high water. Move your car to the upper level, and do not walk on the sea wall while the red flag is flying.
